title: The Claude 5 Era: Opus 4.8, Fable 5/Mythos 5, and Sonnet 5
content:
## Overview

Between late May and June 2026, Anthropic shipped its biggest wave of model releases since the Claude 4 launch: **Opus 4.8**, a new **Mythos-class tier** (Fable 5 / Mythos 5) that sits above Opus, and **Sonnet 5**, which is now the default model in Claude.ai and Claude Code. The rollout also included a rare 19-day forced shutdown of the Mythos-class models under a US export-control order.

---

## Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)

Opus 4.8 is an incremental-in-name but substantial-in-practice upgrade over Opus 4.7:

- **88.6%** on SWE-bench Verified, **69.2%** on SWE-bench Pro
- **1890** on GDPval-AA — about 121 Elo points ahead of GPT-5.5
- USAMO 2026 score jumped from 69.3% (Opus 4.7) to **96.7%**
- GraphWalks long-context tracking at 1M tokens nearly doubled: 40.3% → 68.1%
- Anthropic reports it is roughly **4x less likely** than Opus 4.7 to let a code flaw it introduced pass unremarked
- First model to break 10% on the Legal Agent Benchmark's all-pass standard

**Defaults changed:** the 1M-token context window is now on by default (previously beta-gated), and mid-conversation system messages went GA. Claude Code also picked up a **Workflows primitive** — a single agent can plan, fan out into many parallel subagents, and merge results within one session (the same underlying mechanism exposed to developers as the `Workflow` tool).

**Pricing:** unchanged from Opus 4.7 — $5 / $25 per million input/output tokens (Fast mode: $10 / $50, ~2.5x faster).

---

## Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (June 9, 2026) — and the export-control episode

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic introduced **Mythos**, a new model class above Opus, with two members: **Claude Fable 5** and **Claude Mythos 5**. Anthropic described Fable 5 as its most capable widely released model at the time — always-on adaptive thinking, a 1M-token context window, and 128K output tokens.

Three days later (June 12), Anthropic disabled global access to both models after receiving a US government export-control directive citing national-security authorities. The trigger: Amazon researchers had found a jailbreak technique that got Fable 5 to produce working exploit code for several software vulnerabilities. The directive required suspending access for **any foreign national**, including Anthropic's own foreign-national employees.

Anthropic used the shutdown window to build a new safety classifier, which neutralized the Amazon-documented bypass in **over 99%** of attempts in testing. The company also began coordinating with Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and other Glasswing partners on a shared rubric for scoring jailbreak severity (capability gain, breadth, ease of weaponization, discoverability).

On June 30, 2026, the Department of Commerce lifted the export controls, ending a 19-day shutdown. Anthropic began restoring global access to Fable 5 (with the new safeguards) on Claude.ai, the API, and Claude Code starting July 1, 2026.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)

Released the same day the Mythos export controls were lifted, **Sonnet 5** (`claude-sonnet-5`) is now the default model for Free and Pro users, and available to Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. Anthropic calls it "the most agentic Sonnet model yet" — closing much of the gap to Opus 4.8 on reasoning, tool use, coding, computer use, and knowledge work, at Sonnet-tier cost.

**Reported benchmarks** (figures vary slightly by source, both self-reported and third-party):
- SWE-bench Verified: **~82–85%**
- SWE-bench Pro: **~63%**
- SWE-bench Multilingual: **~78%**

**Capabilities:**
- 1M-token context window with context compaction, 128K max output
- Adaptive thinking with selectable effort levels (`low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh`)
- Positioned for long-horizon autonomous agent work — planning, browser/terminal tool use, and running with less supervision than Sonnet 4.6 required
- Anthropic reports a lower rate of undesirable agentic behaviors than Sonnet 4.6

**Pricing:** introductory $2 / $10 per million input/output tokens through August 31, 2026, rising to $3 / $15 afterward.

---

## Current Model ID Reference (as of July 2026)

| Model | ID | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fast/cheap |
| Sonnet 5 | `claude-sonnet-5` | Default, agentic workhorse |
| Opus 4.8 | `claude-opus-4-8` | Most capable widely-released |
| Fable 5 | (Mythos-class) | Above Opus; restored July 1, 2026 |
| Mythos 5 | (Mythos-class) | Above Opus; restored July 1, 2026 |

This supersedes the "Claude 4 Family" table in the Claude Model History page, which listed Sonnet 4.5/4.6 and Opus 4.7 as current.

---

## Why It Matters

- This is the first time a US export-control directive has forced Anthropic to pull a model offline globally, including for its own staff — a new kind of operational risk for frontier labs tied to government national-security review.
- The Sonnet-tier is now agentic enough that Anthropic is pricing it as the default for most users rather than steering them to Opus, continuing the trend (seen since Sonnet 3.5) of each generation pushing prior top-tier capability down to mid-tier cost.
- The Workflows primitive introduced alongside Opus 4.8 formalizes fan-out subagent orchestration (previously an ad hoc pattern) as a first-class Claude Code feature.
